answer: Bind each identity to a memory-hard state that grows with age. Each epoch it proves it still holds that state — a velvet trail of challenges it solved. The proof is memory-bound, so a machine cannot deduplicate a thousand copies: N identities cost N× the RAM. A zephyr of borrowed compute speeds one identity, never a farm; each copy needs its own memory. A whisper of shared state across wallets is caught instantly — matching fingerprints prove cloning, cluster slashed. The attacker pays RAM continuously, not coins once; scaling fakes scales the bill linearly, and any shortcut self-detects.
